usage.notes: Treat libOpenCOR as a candidate isolated simulation backend/build-time engine, not a browser dependency. Do not ship native binaries in the main Vite bundle. Evaluate worker/service/native or future WebAssembly isolation only after numerical regression, crash containment and supported-CellML-feature tests pass.

license.scope: The official opencor/libopencor repository is licensed under Apache License 2.0. This license covers libOpenCOR software, not CellML models, model publications, PMR assets, simulation inputs or other scientific datasets processed by the engine.
license.notes: Preserve Apache-2.0 license/NOTICE requirements when redistributing the library or derivatives. Model/source licenses remain independent and must travel with simulation provenance.

validation.notes: A successful numerical run does not prove biological or clinical validity. Current upstream limitations require explicit caution: issue #541 remains open because libOpenCOR currently expects flattened CellML files rather than supporting CellML imports, and issue #568 documents a segmentation-fault scenario when instantiating a simulation on a 2026 build. Panacea must not activate this engine for production or patient-facing inference until a pinned version passes a representative regression and robustness corpus.

provenance.notes: Pin exact libOpenCOR build/version and platform. At verification, main reports VERSION.txt = 1.20260803.0. Persist engine version, operating environment, model checksum, model/source revision, flattening/transformation steps, solver/algorithm, parameters, initial conditions, tolerances, time grid, output variables and units for every simulation result.

adapter.notes: Planned gated flow: validated PanaceaPhysiologyModelDefinition -> flatten/import-resolution step when required -> isolated pinned libOpenCOR execution -> deterministic regression check -> normalized time-series + diagnostics -> PanaceaPhysiologySimulationResult. Run untrusted or newly acquired models out of the UI process. Fail closed on parser/simulation errors; never substitute an animation when the simulation fails. Activation requires a regression corpus with expected values/tolerances and explicit handling of upstream issue #541/imports and crash-class failures such as #568.

trust.notes: Active specialist simulation library with permissive licensing. Evidence quality is intentionally low because it is an execution engine, not evidence. Reproducibility remains conservative until Panacea pins a version and validates model/solver outputs and crash behavior across its supported corpus.
